---
title: Duplicate clips
description: Put copies of the selected clips straight after them with one key, or drag copies to exactly where you want them.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Duplicate makes copies of clips without going through the clipboard. Press a key to put them right after the originals, or hold ⌥ and drag them where you want them.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Duplicate"
  keys={['⌘D', '⌥-drag']}
  where="The Duplicate button in the timeline bar"
  tools={['duplicate', 'move_clip']}
/>

## Duplicate the selection

Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. **Edit ▸ Duplicate** and the timeline bar's **Duplicate** button do the same, and both are off with nothing selected.

Each copy goes on the same track as its original, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing: if it runs from 10 s to 14 s, every copy starts 4 s later than its original.

The copies are one undo step, called Duplicate.

## Drag a copy

To place copies somewhere else, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press on a clip, then drag. The copies follow the pointer and the originals stay where they are.

- If the clip you press is part of the selection, the whole selection is copied. If it isn't, only that clip is.
- The copies snap and change tracks as a [move](/editing/move-clips/) does. Drop past the top or bottom of the stack to make a new track for them.
- A drop the timeline can't take springs back, and nothing changes.
- The whole drag is one undo step, called Duplicate Clips.

Hold only <kbd>⌥</kbd>. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on a clip is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a copy.

:::caution
An ⌥-drag makes its copies by duplicating first, so it needs the room a <kbd>⌘D</kbd> would need. If Duplicate [wouldn't work](#when-duplicate-wont-work) at that moment, because the next clip is hard up against the selection, the drag moves the originals instead. Undo it, then [copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) the clip, which has no such limit.
:::

## What a copy keeps

A copy is the whole clip: its source, trim, speed, name, label, picture and sound settings, and actions. From then on it's a clip of its own, so changing one doesn't change the other.

- **Linked clips.** If a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), its partner is copied too and the two copies are linked to each other. A partner on a locked track isn't copied.
- **Nest clips.** A copy of a nest clip made with Duplicate or ⌥-drag shows the same nest as the original, so an edit inside one shows in both. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).

## When Duplicate won't work

Copies follow the same overlap rule as any other placement, and Frame Job doesn't push later clips out of the way.

- A copy may overlap the clip after it by up to half of the shorter clip. The overlap gets a Cross Dissolve, as any new overlap does. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
- A longer overlap stops the duplicate. Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- An adjustment clip can't overlap anything, so a copy of one needs clear space.

To duplicate into a tight edit, open room first or use **Edit ▸ Copy** and **Edit ▸ Paste**. A paste that has no room goes on a new track.

## Related

- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)

---
title: Copy, cut and paste
description: Copy clips to the clipboard and paste them at the playhead, in the same project or another one, keeping their arrangement.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The clipboard carries clips from one place to another: later in the same timeline, or into a different project. Pasted clips land at the playhead and keep the arrangement you copied.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Copy', 'Edit ▸ Cut', 'Edit ▸ Paste']}
  keys={['⌘C', '⌘X', '⌘V']}
  tools="paste"
/>

## Copy and paste clips

<Steps>

1. Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Copy**. The clipboard holds the clips and a note of the media files they show.

2. Move the playhead to where they should go.

3. Press <kbd>⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste**.

</Steps>

The pasted clips are selected, so you can drag or style them straight away. The paste is one undo step, called Paste, and you can paste the same clips as many times as you like.

**Copy** and **Cut** are greyed out with nothing selected. **Paste** needs no selection. It's greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard, because it never pastes another app's text or files.

While you're typing in a field, these keys act on the text in the field, not on clips.

## Cut clips

Press <kbd>⌘X</kbd> or choose **Edit ▸ Cut**. The clips go on the clipboard and are then deleted, leaving gaps, exactly as <kbd>⌫</kbd> does. To close the gaps as well, see [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).

A cut is one undo step, called Cut. If the clips can't be copied, Frame Job beeps and deletes nothing.

## Where pasted clips land

Paste keeps the arrangement you copied.

- **In time.** The earliest clip lands at the playhead, and every other clip keeps its distance from it. Everything lands on a frame.
- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.

## When there's no room

A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.

A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Paste into another project

Copy in one project, then paste in another. Open the other project first or afterwards, either works, because the clips stay on the clipboard.

- **Media.** Files are matched by their path. A file the project already has is reused, and one it doesn't have is added to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Only files the pasted clips use come across, including the `.cube` file of a [look](/color/luts/) and the LUT of [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
- **Frame rate.** Pasted clips are snapped to this project's frame rate.
- **New identities.** Pasted clips are new clips, so they can be pasted again into the project they came from.

A graphic clip brings its name and not its files. In a project without that graphic, the clip draws a red error card until you add a graphic of the same name. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## A detached sound comes along

When a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), selecting its picture copies both, so the pair pastes as a linked pair. Selecting the sound on its own copies only the sound, and it pastes as an ordinary clip with no link to any picture.

Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.

## Copied clips as text

Paste into a text editor and you get a one-line summary of what was copied, in the project's timecode:

```text
Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00
```

## Good to know

:::caution
**Nest clips can't be pasted.** The clipboard holds the nest clip but not what's inside it, so **Paste** shows an error and pastes nothing, even if only one of the copied clips is a nest clip. **Cut** still deletes a nest clip, so press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back. To make another copy of a nest clip, use [Duplicate or ⌥-drag](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
:::

- A paste lands whole or not at all. If one clip can't go in, Frame Job shows an error naming it and nothing changes. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), for example, can't be pasted while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open.
- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.

## With an agent

`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard, at any time and on any track. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

- **In time.** The earliest clip lands at the playhead, and every other clip keeps its distance from it. Everything lands on a frame.
- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.

## When there's no room

A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.

A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Paste into another project

Copy in one project, then paste in another. Open the other project first or afterwards, either works, because the clips stay on the clipboard.

- **Media.** Files are matched by their path. A file the project already has is reused, and one it doesn't have is added to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Only files the pasted clips use come across, including the `.cube` file of a [look](/color/luts/) and the LUT of [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
- **Frame rate.** Pasted clips are snapped to this project's frame rate.
- **New identities.** Pasted clips are new clips, so they can be pasted again into the project they came from.

A graphic clip brings its name and not its files. In a project without that graphic, the clip draws a red error card until you add a graphic of the same name. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## A detached sound comes along

When a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), selecting its picture copies both, so the pair pastes as a linked pair. Selecting the sound on its own copies only the sound, and it pastes as an ordinary clip with no link to any picture.

Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.

## Copied clips as text

Paste into a text editor and you get a one-line summary of what was copied, in the project's timecode:

```text
Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00
```

## Good to know

:::caution
**Nest clips can't be pasted.** The clipboard holds the nest clip but not what's inside it, so **Paste** shows an error and pastes nothing, even if only one of the copied clips is a nest clip. **Cut** still deletes a nest clip, so press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back. To make another copy of a nest clip, use [Duplicate or ⌥-drag](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
:::

- A paste lands whole or not at all. If one clip can't go in, Frame Job shows an error naming it and nothing changes. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), for example, can't be pasted while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open.
- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.

## With an agent

`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard, at any time and on any track. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)

---
title: Paste Attributes
description: Copy one clip's look and sound settings onto any number of other clips in a single step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Paste Attributes makes other clips look and sound like the one you copied. Set up one clip, then give the same settings to the rest in one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
  keys="⌥⌘V"
  tools="paste_attributes"
/>

## Paste a clip's attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take them.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The item is on when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.

If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.

## What travels

Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.

Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.

| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing |
| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |

:::caution
The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
:::

A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.

## What stays on the target

Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:

- its place on the timeline and its length
- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
- its transition
- its name and label
- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)

Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.

## Adjustment clips and qualifiers

A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.

## When a paste stops

Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error naming the clip and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.

| The target | Can't take |
| --- | --- |
| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
| A movie or still clip | Remove Background set to a subject only image clips have, Foreground |
| Any clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |

To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things the menu item can't. It can name which groups travel, so it can paste the sound alone and leave the picture settings. And with groups named, it can paste across a mixed selection without stopping, skipping any clip that can't take a group. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)

---
title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
  tools="set_enabled"
/>

## Turn a half off

There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:

| Command | What it switches |
| --- | --- |
| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
| [**Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |

To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

## How the clip looks

| Switched off | On the timeline |
| --- | --- |
| The picture of a movie clip | It reads as an audio clip, with the audio tint and symbol, and has no filmstrip. |
| The sound | It has no waveform. |
| Both | It's dimmed, like a clip on a hidden track. |

A clip with its sound off has no **Sound** tab in the inspector, because there's nothing there to adjust. Its **Picture** tab stays, even with the picture off.

## Good to know

- A clip with its sound off can't be transcribed, and **Remove Silences** doesn't count it as audible.
- Copies keep the switches of the clip they came from.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) leaves the target's switches alone.

## With an agent

`set_enabled` switches either half of any clip directly, which no command in the app does on its own. Leave a half out to keep it as it is. See [Tools: move and trim](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

## Related

- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)

---
title: Nests
description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
/>

## Make a nest

<Steps>

1. Select the clips.

2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.

</Steps>

The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.

The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).

A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.

To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).

## What a nest keeps

Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.

The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:

- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.

The nest clip itself starts with a plain transform at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.

## Name a nest

Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.

A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.

## A nest's size is fixed

A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the [project's size](/projects/canvas-size/) later doesn't re-lay out what's inside, and opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.

To change a nest's size:

<Steps>

1. Press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it.

2. Change the project size if you need to.

3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd> to nest it again.

</Steps>

## Un-nest

Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is on when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.

Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.

- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
- A clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).

:::caution
Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
:::

The states of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Returning clips take on the timeline tracks they land on.

## Nests inside nests

A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.

The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.

## When Nest won't work

**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.

Two things stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.

- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the overlap rule allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.

If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## With an agent

`nest` can name the nest as it's made, and `get_project` lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)

Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is on when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.

Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.

- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
- A clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).

:::caution
Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
:::

The states of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Returning clips take on the timeline tracks they land on.

## Nests inside nests

A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.

The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.

## When Nest won't work

**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.

Two things stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.

- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the overlap rule allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.

If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## With an agent

`nest` can name the nest as it's made, and `get_project` lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: Duplicate clips
description: Put copies of the selected clips straight after them with one key, or drag copies to exactly where you want them.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Duplicate makes copies of clips without going through the clipboard. Press a key to put them right after the originals, or hold ⌥ and drag them where you want them.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Duplicate"
  keys={['⌘D', '⌥-drag']}
  where="The Duplicate button in the timeline bar"
  tools={['duplicate', 'move_clip']}
/>

## Duplicate the selection

Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. **Edit ▸ Duplicate** and the timeline bar's **Duplicate** button do the same, and both are off with nothing selected.

Each copy goes on the same track as its original, starting right after the selection's span. A selection of several clips keeps its internal timing: if it runs from 10 s to 14 s, every copy starts 4 s later than its original.

The copies are one undo step, called Duplicate.

## Drag a copy

To place copies somewhere else, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press on a clip, then drag. The copies follow the pointer and the originals stay where they are.

- If the clip you press is part of the selection, the whole selection is copied. If it isn't, only that clip is.
- The copies snap and change tracks as a [move](/editing/move-clips/) does. Drop past the top or bottom of the stack to make a new track for them.
- A drop the timeline can't take springs back, and nothing changes.
- The whole drag is one undo step, called Duplicate Clips.

Hold only <kbd>⌥</kbd>. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on a clip is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a copy.

:::caution
An ⌥-drag makes its copies by duplicating first, so it needs the room a <kbd>⌘D</kbd> would need. If Duplicate [wouldn't work](#when-duplicate-wont-work) at that moment, because the next clip is hard up against the selection, the drag moves the originals instead. Undo it, then [copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) the clip, which has no such limit.
:::

## What a copy keeps

A copy is the whole clip: its source, trim, speed, name, label, picture and sound settings, and actions. From then on it's a clip of its own, so changing one doesn't change the other.

- **Linked clips.** If a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), its partner is copied too and the two copies are linked to each other. A partner on a locked track isn't copied.
- **Nest clips.** A copy of a nest clip made with Duplicate or ⌥-drag shows the same nest as the original, so an edit inside one shows in both. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).

## When Duplicate won't work

Copies follow the same overlap rule as any other placement, and Frame Job doesn't push later clips out of the way.

- A copy may overlap the clip after it by up to half of the shorter clip. The overlap gets a Cross Dissolve, as any new overlap does. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
- A longer overlap stops the duplicate. Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- An adjustment clip can't overlap anything, so a copy of one needs clear space.

To duplicate into a tight edit, open room first or use **Edit ▸ Copy** and **Edit ▸ Paste**. A paste that has no room goes on a new track.

## Related

- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)

---
title: Copy, cut and paste
description: Copy clips to the clipboard and paste them at the playhead, in the same project or another one, keeping their arrangement.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The clipboard carries clips from one place to another: later in the same timeline, or into a different project. Pasted clips land at the playhead and keep the arrangement you copied.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Edit ▸ Copy', 'Edit ▸ Cut', 'Edit ▸ Paste']}
  keys={['⌘C', '⌘X', '⌘V']}
  tools="paste"
/>

## Copy and paste clips

<Steps>

1. Select the clips and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Copy**. The clipboard holds the clips and a note of the media files they show.

2. Move the playhead to where they should go.

3. Press <kbd>⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste**.

</Steps>

The pasted clips are selected, so you can drag or style them straight away. The paste is one undo step, called Paste, and you can paste the same clips as many times as you like.

**Copy** and **Cut** are greyed out with nothing selected. **Paste** needs no selection. It's greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard, because it never pastes another app's text or files.

While you're typing in a field, these keys act on the text in the field, not on clips.

## Cut clips

Press <kbd>⌘X</kbd> or choose **Edit ▸ Cut**. The clips go on the clipboard and are then deleted, leaving gaps, exactly as <kbd>⌫</kbd> does. To close the gaps as well, see [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).

A cut is one undo step, called Cut. If the clips can't be copied, Frame Job beeps and deletes nothing.

## Where pasted clips land

Paste keeps the arrangement you copied.

- **In time.** The earliest clip lands at the playhead, and every other clip keeps its distance from it. Everything lands on a frame.
- **Across tracks.** Each clip keeps its place in the stack, counted back from the front. A clip copied from the front track lands on the front track, and one copied from the second track down lands on the second track down. A selection across two lanes pastes back onto two lanes.
- **Missing tracks.** If the project has too few tracks, new ones are added at the back.

## When there's no room

A paste isn't turned down for lack of room. A clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track at the front, so it stays visible over what was already there.

A smaller overlap is allowed, as it is for any placement: up to half of the shorter clip. The clip stays on its track and the overlap gets a Cross Dissolve. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Paste into another project

Copy in one project, then paste in another. Open the other project first or afterwards, either works, because the clips stay on the clipboard.

- **Media.** Files are matched by their path. A file the project already has is reused, and one it doesn't have is added to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Only files the pasted clips use come across, including the `.cube` file of a [look](/color/luts/) and the LUT of [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
- **Frame rate.** Pasted clips are snapped to this project's frame rate.
- **New identities.** Pasted clips are new clips, so they can be pasted again into the project they came from.

A graphic clip brings its name and not its files. In a project without that graphic, the clip draws a red error card until you add a graphic of the same name. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

## A detached sound comes along

When a clip has a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), selecting its picture copies both, so the pair pastes as a linked pair. Selecting the sound on its own copies only the sound, and it pastes as an ordinary clip with no link to any picture.

Cut follows the same split. Cutting a picture takes its sound with it, unless the sound is on a locked track. Cutting a detached sound on its own leaves the picture in place, silent.

## Copied clips as text

Paste into a text editor and you get a one-line summary of what was copied, in the project's timecode:

```text
Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00
```

## Good to know

:::caution
**Nest clips can't be pasted.** The clipboard holds the nest clip but not what's inside it, so **Paste** shows an error and pastes nothing, even if only one of the copied clips is a nest clip. **Cut** still deletes a nest clip, so press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> to bring it back. To make another copy of a nest clip, use [Duplicate or ⌥-drag](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
:::

- A paste lands whole or not at all. If one clip can't go in, Frame Job shows an error naming it and nothing changes. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), for example, can't be pasted while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open.
- Room for a paste isn't unlimited: a project holds up to 64 tracks and 4,096 clips. A paste that would pass either limit shows an error.
- Copy and Paste work inside a nest. **Copy** takes the clips you picked and counts their depth against the nest's own tracks, and **Paste** lands in the nest that's open.

## With an agent

`paste` takes a description of the clips in the same form Copy writes, so an agent can place clips without touching your clipboard, at any time and on any track. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

---
title: Paste Attributes
description: Copy one clip's look and sound settings onto any number of other clips in a single step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Paste Attributes makes other clips look and sound like the one you copied. Set up one clip, then give the same settings to the rest in one undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
  keys="⌥⌘V"
  tools="paste_attributes"
/>

## Paste a clip's attributes

<Steps>

1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips that should take them.

3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.

</Steps>

The item is on when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.

If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.

## What travels

Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.

Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.

| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing |
| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |

:::caution
The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
:::

A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.

## What stays on the target

Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:

- its place on the timeline and its length
- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
- its transition
- its name and label
- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)

Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.

## Adjustment clips and qualifiers

A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:

| Pasting | The qualifier |
| --- | --- |
| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |

See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.

## When a paste stops

Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error naming the clip and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.

| The target | Can't take |
| --- | --- |
| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
| A movie or still clip | Remove Background set to a subject only image clips have, Foreground |
| Any clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |

To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things the menu item can't. It can name which groups travel, so it can paste the sound alone and leave the picture settings. And with groups named, it can paste across a mixed selection without stopping, skipping any clip that can't take a group. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)
- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)
- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)

---
title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
  tools="set_enabled"
/>

## Turn a half off

There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:

| Command | What it switches |
| --- | --- |
| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
| [**Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |

To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

## How the clip looks

| Switched off | On the timeline |
| --- | --- |
| The picture of a movie clip | It reads as an audio clip, with the audio tint and symbol, and has no filmstrip. |
| The sound | It has no waveform. |
| Both | It's dimmed, like a clip on a hidden track. |

A clip with its sound off has no **Sound** tab in the inspector, because there's nothing there to adjust. Its **Picture** tab stays, even with the picture off.

## Good to know

- A clip with its sound off can't be transcribed, and **Remove Silences** doesn't count it as audible.
- Copies keep the switches of the clip they came from.
- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) leaves the target's switches alone.

## With an agent

`set_enabled` switches either half of any clip directly, which no command in the app does on its own. Leave a half out to keep it as it is. See [Tools: move and trim](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).

## Related

- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)

---
title: Nests
description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
/>

## Make a nest

<Steps>

1. Select the clips.

2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.

</Steps>

The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.

The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).

A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.

To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).

## What a nest keeps

Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.

The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:

- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.

The nest clip itself starts with a plain transform at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.

## Name a nest

Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.

A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.

## A nest's size is fixed

A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the [project's size](/projects/canvas-size/) later doesn't re-lay out what's inside, and opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.

To change a nest's size:

<Steps>

1. Press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it.

2. Change the project size if you need to.

3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd> to nest it again.

</Steps>

## Un-nest

Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is on when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.

Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.

- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
- A clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).

:::caution
Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
:::

The states of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Returning clips take on the timeline tracks they land on.

## Nests inside nests

A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.

The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.

## When Nest won't work

**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.

Two things stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.

- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the overlap rule allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.

If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## With an agent

`nest` can name the nest as it's made, and `get_project` lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. See [Tools: copy and nest](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

All 27 features are covered. check-pages and docs_site_proof report 0 problems on the five pages. Anchors are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevingalligan-devel-framejob/9cfd7405-83ec-4caa-905f-7b97a20f2cc9/scratchpad/inventory/anchors/editing-3.json and match the brief's ids exactly. I did not run pnpm build, so link anchors are unchecked by a build; the one in-page anchor I link (#when-duplicate-wont-work) exists.

Where the code contradicts the guide or the brief (the pages follow the code):

1. Copying and pasting a nest clip fails. This is from reading the code; I did not run it in the app, to avoid touching the owner's clipboard. Copy's clipboard payload (EditorViewController+Clipboard.swift) holds only "clips" and "media", never "nests", and the core's paste errors on a nest clip whose nest the payload lacks (core test pasting_a_nest_clip_whose_nest_is_missing_is_an_error). So Paste shows an error, and Cut still deletes the nest clip (undo restores it). docs/guide/editing.md says Copy and Paste make an independent copy. This looks like a real app bug: the core supports a "nests" key and has a test for it, but Swift never writes it. editing/copy-and-paste documents the real behaviour in a caution. The page editing/nest-copies is not in my brief; if it repeats the guide's claim it will contradict this one. Someone should reconcile the two and consider filing an issue.

2. ⌥-drag falls back to a plain move when Duplicate would be refused, for example when the next clip butts against the selection (TimelineView.beginClipDrag: a failed probe leaves no copies). The guide doesn't mention this. It's documented as a caution on editing/duplicate-clips.

3. Paste depth is counted from the front of the source's whole track stack, not from the front-most lane copied. A clip copied from the second track down lands on the second track down, so the guide's "copied front-most lane goes onto the front track" is only true when the copy includes the front track. Pages follow the code.

4. The brief says Detach Audio is the app's only control for a clip's halves. Attach Audio and Switch by Speaker also change them, and the enable page lists all three.

5. Paste Attributes' Video group also carries motion presets (the In, Out and During slots), which the brief doesn't list. Actions stay on the target.

6. The catalog says an empty groups list is refused; the core's doc comment says it is an identity. I didn't settle this, as it belongs on the MCP page, and my pages don't state it.

The red error card for a pasted graphic in a project without its module rests on the guide plus the existence of error cards in the code; I did not trace that exact path.
